section_1.title: Introduction: The Infinite Spinner
section_1.content: Introduce the physical metaphor of the windmill. Imagine a set of 'stars' (points) on a map and a 'laser beam' (line) that rotates. Hook the audience with the central mystery: If this beam keeps spinning and switching its pivot point, will it hit every star eventually?
section_1.example: A tiny robot named 'Dusty' stands on a point in a field of 5 scattered points. He holds a long pole and starts spinning clockwise. When the pole hits another point, Dusty jumps to that new point and keeps spinning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game
section_2.content: Define the mathematical constraints clearly to avoid edge cases. Explain 'General Position' (no three points are collinear) and the 'Pivot' mechanism. Use visuals to show a line rotating around a fixed center until it intersects exactly one other point.
section_2.example: Visual: 3 points arranged in a triangle. Show the line rotating 60 degrees from point A to point B. If three points were in a straight line, the robot wouldn't know which one to jump to first!

section_3.title: The Mechanism of the Pivot
section_3.content: Demonstrate the transition. When the line hits a new point, the 'pivot' point changes. Emphasize that the rotation direction (clockwise) never changes. Animate the line 'sweeping' through the plane like a radar.
section_3.example: Graphical Animation: A blue line pivots on Point P. As it rotates, it strikes Point Q. The center of rotation instantly shifts from P to Q, and the line continues its clockwise sweep from its new position.

section_4.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
section_4.content: Introduce the core insight needed to solve the problem: The 'Side-Count'. If we choose a line that splits the points into two equal (or near-equal) sets, what happens to that count when the line pivots?
section_4.example: Visual: Color points on the 'left' side of the line Blue and points on the 'right' side Red. When the line pivots on Point P to hit Point Q, Point P moves to the other side of the line, and Point Q moves to the pivot. The total number of points on each side stays exactly the same!

section_5.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_5.content: Explain the global behavior. After the line has rotated 180 degrees, it returns to its original orientation but is 'flipped'. Every point that was on the left is now on the right, and vice versa. This transition proves that the line must have passed through every point to 'swap' their positions.
section_5.example: Imagine 5 points. The line starts with 2 points on the left and 2 on the right. After a half-rotation (180°), the 2 points that were on the left MUST have been crossed to end up on the right. Since this applies to any point, the 'Windmill' must visit everyone.

section_6.title: Conclusion and Application
section_6.content: Summarize the beauty of the problem: how a simple local rule (rotating and hitting points) leads to a predictable global outcome. Mention that this was the 'hardest' problem of the 2011 International Mathematical Olympiad, yet its solution is purely visual logic.
section_6.example: Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill completing a full 360-degree cycle, highlighting how each point takes its turn as the 'heart' (pivot) of the system.

section_2.example: Visual: 3 points arranged in a triangle. Show the line rotating 60 degrees from point A to point B. If three points were in a straight line, the robot wouldn't know which one to jump to first!

section_3.title: The Mechanism of the Pivot
section_3.content: Demonstrate the transition. When the line hits a new point, the 'pivot' point changes. Emphasize that the rotation direction (clockwise) never changes. Animate the line 'sweeping' through the plane like a radar.
section_3.example: Graphical Animation: A blue line pivots on Point P. As it rotates, it strikes Point Q. The center of rotation instantly shifts from P to Q, and the line continues its clockwise sweep from its new position.

section_4.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
section_4.content: Introduce the core insight needed to solve the problem: The 'Side-Count'. If we choose a line that splits the points into two equal (or near-equal) sets, what happens to that count when the line pivots?
section_4.example: Visual: Color points on the 'left' side of the line Blue and points on the 'right' side Red. When the line pivots on Point P to hit Point Q, Point P moves to the other side of the line, and Point Q moves to the pivot. The total number of points on each side stays exactly the same!

section_5.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_5.content: Explain the global behavior. After the line has rotated 180 degrees, it returns to its original orientation but is 'flipped'. Every point that was on the left is now on the right, and vice versa. This transition proves that the line must have passed through every point to 'swap' their positions.
section_5.example: Imagine 5 points. The line starts with 2 points on the left and 2 on the right. After a half-rotation (180°), the 2 points that were on the left MUST have been crossed to end up on the right. Since this applies to any point, the 'Windmill' must visit everyone.

section_6.title: Conclusion and Application
section_6.content: Summarize the beauty of the problem: how a simple local rule (rotating and hitting points) leads to a predictable global outcome. Mention that this was the 'hardest' problem of the 2011 International Mathematical Olympiad, yet its solution is purely visual logic.
section_6.example: Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill completing a full 360-degree cycle, highlighting how each point takes its turn as the 'heart' (pivot) of the system.

section_1.title: Introduction: The Infinite Spinner
lecture_lines: Imagine points like stars scattered across a map.
We place a rotating line through one central point.
As the line spins, it strikes another point.
The pivot point then jumps to this new star.
Can this simple dance visit every single point?
animations: Fade in 5 points at random positions (color: #FFFFFF). self.wait(1.5).
Create a long line through a central point (color: #FFD700). self.wait(2.0).
Rotate the line clockwise; when it hits another point, flash that point (color: #00FF00). self.wait(1.5).
Shift the line's pivot point to the hit point and continue rotation. self.wait(2.0).
Highlight all points with a pulsing glow to indicate potential visitation (color: #FF4500). self.wait(2.0).

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game
lecture_lines: No three points lie on a single straight line.
The line rotates until it strikes exactly one point.
The pivot immediately shifts to this new point.
animations: Show 3 points in a triangle (#FFFFFF); draw a line through two and show a red 'X' to indicate invalidity. self.wait(2.0).
Show a line rotating clockwise around a single pivot point (color: #FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line until it strikes exactly one new point; highlight the intersection (color: #00FF00). self.wait(2.0).

section_3.title: The Mechanism of the Pivot
lecture_lines: Watch the line sweep across the plane like radar.
Upon impact, the center of rotation instantly changes.
The clockwise motion remains constant throughout the dance.
animations: Animate the line sweeping clockwise like a radar beam, leaving a faint trail (color: #FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
When the line hits a point, shift the pivot point instantly and flash the new pivot (color: #00FF00). self.wait(2.0).
Continue the clockwise sweep from the new pivot position without pause. self.wait(1.5).

section_4.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
lecture_lines: Color points on each side of the line differently.
Pick a line splitting points into two equal sets.
As the line pivots, points swap sides across it.
The current pivot and the new pivot trade places.
The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced.
animations: Draw a balanced line through a pivot with 2 blue points (#0000FF) on the left and 2 red points (#FF0000) on the right. self.wait(2.0).
Use blue and red SurroundingRectangles to group the points on either side. self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line; show the current pivot moving to the other side as the new point becomes the pivot. self.wait(2.0).
Use Arrows to show the points effectively exchanging places relative to the line. self.wait(1.5).
Flash the blue and red groups to show the total counts (2 on each side) remain unchanged. self.wait(2.0).

section_5.title: The 180-Degree Flip
lecture_lines: After a half-rotation, the line returns to its angle.
However, the line is now oriented in reverse.
Points originally on the left are now on the right.
Every point must cross the line to swap sides.
This proves the windmill hits every star eventually.
animations: Show the initial balanced line with labeled sides and colored points (#0000FF and #FF0000). self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line slowly 180 degrees using a 'smooth' rate function (color: #FFD700). self.wait(3.0).
Morph the side labels and point colors to show the sides have completely swapped. self.wait(2.0).
Highlight each point in sequence as the line passes through it during the rotation. self.wait(1.5).
Flash all points in green (#00FF00) to signify the proof is complete. self.wait(2.0).

section_6.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Local rules create a beautiful, predictable global cycle.
This visual logic solved the hardest IMO 2011 problem.
Simple rotations reveal deep truths in geometry and combinatorics.
animations: Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill completing a full cycle. self.wait(2.0).
Display the text 'IMO 2011 Problem 2' in gold (#FFD700). self.wait(1.5).
Fade out the points and line into a final geometric pattern. self.wait(2.0).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

from manim import *

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Dim all lecture lines initially for emphasis
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color("#444444")
            
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        title_text = "Introduction: The Infinite Spinner"

            "As the line spins, it strikes another point.",
            "The pivot point then jumps to this new star.",
            "Can this simple dance visit every single point?"
        ]

        p5_pos = self.grid['B5']

            Dot(p2_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p3_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p4_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p5_pos, color="#FFFFFF")

            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            return [pivot_pt - direction * 4.5, pivot_pt + direction * 4.5]

        target_angle_2 = np.arctan2(-1.0, -2.0)

The code for **Section 2: Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game** has been implemented. 

### Key Features:
- **Visual Anchor System**: Used the mandatory 6x6 grid (`A1-F6`) for all positioning, ensuring visuals remain on the right side and do not obstruct the lecture text.
- **Rule Demonstration**: 
    - **General Position**: Visualized the "no three points collinear" rule by showing a triangle that morphs into a collinear state, marked with a red 'X' to indicate invalidity.
    - **Pivot Mechanism**: Used a `ValueTracker` and `add_updater` to simulate the clockwise rotation of the "windmill" line around a pivot.
    - **Pivot Shift**: Demonstrated the shift of the pivot point to a new intersection point with a color transition to `#00FF00` (Green) and a highlight using `Indicate`.
- **Pedagogical Pacing**: Integrated explicit `self.wait()` calls (1.5-2.0s) between lecture highlights and animation sequences to allow for learner absorption.
- **Consistency**: Used consistent hexadecimal colors (`#FFFFFF`, `#FFD700`, `#00FF00`, `#FF0000`) and linked lecture line highlights to the corresponding animation colors.

The section is designed to render efficiently within the MAS runtime budget by using simple mobjects and minimal updater logic.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF").to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"• {line}", font_size=22, color="#FFFFFF") for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "No three points lie on a single straight line.",
            "The line rotates until it strikes exactly one point.",
            "The pivot immediately shifts to this new point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED_COLOR)
        
        # Show 3 points in a triangle then make them collinear to show invalidity
        p1 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p2 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p3 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Start in triangle
        self.place_at_grid(p1, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(p2, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(p3, "D3")
        
        points = VGroup(p1, p2, p3)
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Move to collinear position (B3, B4, B5) to demonstrate the "invalid" condition
        self.play(
            p1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]),
            p2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            p3.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Draw invalid line and X
        invalid_line = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], color=RED_COLOR)
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT + UP, RIGHT + DOWN, color=RED_COLOR),
            Line(LEFT + DOWN, RIGHT + UP, color=RED_COLOR)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(self.grid["B4"])
        
        self.play(Create(invalid_line))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(points), FadeOut(invalid_line), FadeOut(cross))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # Setup for rotation
        pivot_dot = Dot(color=GOLD_COLOR)
        target_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        other_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_dot, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(other_dot, "B5")
        
        # Rotation mechanics
        # Starting angle slightly counter-clockwise from target
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5) 
        
        # The line rotates clockwise around a single pivot point
        windmill_line = Line(LEFT * 4, RIGHT * 4, color=GOLD_COLOR)
        windmill_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_dot.get_center()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pivot_dot), FadeIn(target_dot), FadeIn(other_dot))
        self.add(windmill_line)
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Target angle calculation (D5 relative to C3)
        # C3 is (2.5, 0.2), D5 is (4.5, -0.8)
        # dx = 2.0, dy = -1.0
        target_angle = np.arctan2(-1.0, 2.0)
        
        # Rotate clockwise (decrease angle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_COLOR)
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: Pacing after significant transition
        
        # Highlight intersection
        self.play(Indicate(target_dot, color=GREEN_COLOR))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Pivot immediately shifts to this new point
        # We move the pivot dot and transition the line color
        self.play(
            pivot_dot.animate.move_to(target_dot.get_center()),
            windmill_line.animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR),
            FadeOut(target_dot, run_time=0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # New line rotation around the new pivot
        windmill_line.clear_updaters()
        windmill_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_dot.get_center()))
        
        # Continue clockwise rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle - 1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Final cleanup/reset colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from shared state
        title = "The 180-Degree Flip"
        lecture_lines = [
            "After a half-rotation, the line returns to its angle.",
            "However, the line is now oriented in reverse.",
            "Points originally on the left are now on the right.",
            "Every point must cross the line to swap sides.",
            "This proves the windmill hits every star eventually."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        BLUE_PT = "#0000FF"
        RED_PT = "#FF0000"
        GOLD_LINE = "#FFD700"
        GREEN_PT = "#00FF00"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the initial balanced line with labeled sides and colored points
        
        # Using specific grid points for clear visual distribution
        pivot_pos = self.grid["D4"]
        pivot_dot = Dot(pivot_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        
        # Left points (Blue) - positioned to be hit during rotation
        p1 = Dot(self.grid["B2"], color=BLUE_PT, radius=0.08)
        p2 = Dot(self.grid["C2"], color=BLUE_PT, radius=0.08)
        
        # Right points (Red)
        p3 = Dot(self.grid["E5"], color=RED_PT, radius=0.08)
        p4 = Dot(self.grid["F5"], color=RED_PT, radius=0.08)
        
        points = VGroup(pivot_dot, p1, p2, p3, p4)
        
        # Initial line (start pointing UP at PI/2)
        line = Line(pivot_pos + DOWN*3.5, pivot_pos + UP*3.5, color=GOLD_LINE, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Side labels
        label_l = Text("L", font_size=24, color=BLUE_PT)
        label_r = Text("R", font_size=24, color=RED_PT)
        
        # Manual positioning within 1 unit for consistency (relative to pivot center initially)
        label_l.move_to(pivot_pos + LEFT * 1.2)
        label_r.move_to(pivot_pos + RIGHT * 1.2)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        self.play(FadeIn(points), Create(line), Write(label_l), Write(label_r))
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rotate the line slowly 180 degrees using a 'smooth' rate function
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def line_updater(m):
            # Line rotates around pivot_pos
            # Angle PI/2 is vertical UP
            angle = PI/2 + angle_tracker.get_value()
            start = pivot_pos - 3.5 * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            end = pivot_pos + 3.5 * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            m.put_start_and_end_on(start, end)
            
        def labels_updater(vgroup):
            # Move labels with the rotation to stay perpendicular to the line
            angle = PI/2 + angle_tracker.get_value()
            # Calculate normal vector (the "left" side relative to line direction)
            normal = np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            vgroup[0].move_to(pivot_pos + normal * 1.2)
            vgroup[1].move_to(pivot_pos - normal * 1.2)
            
        labels_vgroup = VGroup(label_l, label_r)
        line.add_updater(line_updater)
        labels_vgroup.add_updater(labels_updater)
        
        # Perform 180-degree rotation (PI radians)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=5, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(3.0)
        
        line.clear_updaters()
        labels_vgroup.clear_updaters()
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Morph the side labels and point colors to show the sides have completely swapped.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_PT)
        
        # Swap colors visually to represent the change in state
        # Points that were on the left (L/Blue) side of the line are now on the right side
        self.play(
            p1.animate.set_color(RED_PT),
            p2.animate.set_color(RED_PT),
            p3.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            p4.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            label_l.animate.set_color(RED_PT),
            label_r.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight each point in sequence as the line passes through it during the rotation.
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        
        # Indicate points in order of being 'visited' by the line
        self.play(Indicate(p2, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p1, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p3, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p4, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Flash all points in green (#00FF00) to signify the proof is complete.
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN_PT)
        
        # Final flourish
        self.play(
            *[Flash(p, color=GREEN_PT) for p in points],
            *[p.animate.set_color(GREEN_PT) for p in points],
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2.0)

        def get_line_endpoints(pivot_pt, angle):
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            return [pivot_pt - direction * 4.5, pivot_pt + direction * 4.5]

        windmill_line = Line(
            *get_line_endpoints(current_pivot, angle_tracker.get_value()),
            color="#FFD700"
        )
        
        # Use an updater to keep the line centered on the current pivot and at the correct angle
        def windmill_updater(mob):
            new_pts = get_line_endpoints(current_pivot, angle_tracker.get_value())
            mob.set_points_as_corners(new_pts)
            
        windmill_line.add_updater(windmill_updater)

        self.place_at_grid(pivot_p, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_2, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(red_1, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(red_2, 'D5')
        
        all_points = VGroup(pivot_p, blue_1, blue_2, red_1, red_2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color points on each side of the line differently.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        # Initial vertical line passing through the pivot
        windmill_line = Line(
            self.grid['A3'] + UP*0.3, 
            self.grid['F3'] + DOWN*0.3, 
            color=WHITE_CLR
        )
        
        self.add(all_points)
        self.play(Create(windmill_line))
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: absorption time

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pick a line splitting points into two equal sets.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        blue_group = VGroup(blue_1, blue_2)
        red_group = VGroup(red_1, red_2)
        
        # Use SurroundingRectangles to group points visually
        rect_blue = SurroundingRectangle(blue_group, color=BLUE_CLR, buff=0.2)
        rect_red = SurroundingRectangle(red_group, color=RED_CLR, buff=0.2)
        
        # Count labels
        blue_count = Text("2", color=BLUE_CLR, font_size=24)
        red_count = Text("2", color=RED_CLR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(blue_count, 'A2')
        self.place_at_grid(red_count, 'A4')
        
        self.play(Create(rect_blue), Create(rect_red))
        self.play(Write(blue_count), Write(red_count))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # As the line pivots, points swap sides across it.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(rect_blue), FadeOut(rect_red))
        
        # Use ValueTracker for smooth rotation to minimize complexity (L027)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updater for the windmill line to rotate around pivot_p
        def line_updater(l):
            current_angle = PI/2 - angle_tracker.get_value()
            center = pivot_p.get_center()
            dir_vec = np.array([np.cos(current_angle), np.sin(current_angle), 0])
            l.set_points_by_ends(center - dir_vec * 3, center + dir_vec * 3)

        windmill_line.add_updater(line_updater)
        
        # Rotate clockwise to hit red_1 at B4 (45 degrees = PI/4)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/4), run_time=2.5)
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The current pivot and the new pivot trade places.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        # Visualizing the trade with arrows as per storyboard
        arrow_trade_1 = Arrow(self.grid['B4'], self.grid['C3'], color=WHITE_CLR, buff=0.1)
        arrow_trade_2 = Arrow(self.grid['C3'], self.grid['C4'], color=RED_CLR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_trade_1), GrowArrow(arrow_trade_2))
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Update point roles: old pivot becomes red, red_1 becomes new pivot
        self.play(
            pivot_p.animate.set_color(RED_CLR),
            red_1.animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR),
            FadeOut(arrow_trade_1), FadeOut(arrow_trade_2)
        )
        
        # Switch the line's pivot point to the new point red_1
        windmill_line.remove_updater(line_updater)
        
        def line_updater_new(l):
            current_angle = PI/2 - angle_tracker.get_value()
            center = red_1.get_center()
            dir_vec = np.array([np.cos(current_angle), np.sin(current_angle), 0])
            l.set_points_by_ends(center - dir_vec * 3, center + dir_vec * 3)
            
        windmill_line.add_updater(line_updater_new)
        
        # Continue slight rotation to show it's now pivoting around the new point
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.increment_value(PI/8), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        # New groupings: Blue side (blue_1, blue_2), Red side (pivot_p, red_2)
        new_blue_group = VGroup(blue_1, blue_2)
        new_red_group = VGroup(pivot_p, red_2)
        
        rect_blue_final = SurroundingRectangle(new_blue_group, color=BLUE_CLR, buff=0.2)
        rect_red_final = SurroundingRectangle(new_red_group, color=RED_CLR, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_blue_final), Create(rect_red_final))
        # Pulse counts to emphasize the invariant (L004)
        self.play(Indicate(blue_count), Indicate(red_count))
        self.wait(2.0)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

# === Base TeachingScene Class ===
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        title_text = "Conclusion and Application"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Local rules create a beautiful, predictable global cycle.",
            "- This visual logic solved the hardest IMO 2011 problem.",
            "- Simple rotations reveal deep truths in geometry and combinatorics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill completing a full cycle. self.wait(2.0).
        
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF") # Cyan
        
        # Define 10 points in the visual area (B2 to F6)
        point_coords = [
            self.grid["B3"] + [0.2, 0.3, 0],
            self.grid["B5"] + [-0.1, -0.2, 0],
            self.grid["C2"] + [0.4, 0.1, 0],

            self.grid["F5"] + [-0.1, -0.5, 0],
        ]
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(coord, color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) for coord in point_coords])
        self.add(points)
        
        # Initial pivot point
        pivot_idx = 2 # Start at C2
        pivot_dot = points[pivot_idx]
        pivot_dot.set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta for pivot
        
        # Rotating line
        line = Line(pivot_dot.get_center() - 2.5*RIGHT, pivot_dot.get_center() + 2.5*RIGHT, color="#FFFFFF")
        line.set_stroke(width=2)
        self.add(line)
        
        # Fast-motion pivot sequence simulation
        pivots_seq = [5, 7, 1, 9, 0] # Sequence of indices for "hitting" points
        for next_p in pivots_seq:
            # Rotate around current pivot
            self.play(Rotate(line, angle=PI/2, about_point=points[pivot_idx].get_center()), run_time=0.3, rate_func=linear)
            # Switch pivot "instantly"
            self.play(
                points[pivot_idx].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
                points[next_p].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
                line.animate.move_to(points[next_p].get_center()),
                run_time=0.1
            )
            pivot_idx = next_p
            
        # Final rotation to finish the "cycle"
        self.play(Rotate(line, angle=PI, about_point=points[pivot_idx].get_center()), run_time=0.5, rate_func=linear)

            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), # Gold
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        imo_text = Text("IMO 2011 Problem 2", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(imo_text, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(imo_text))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out the points and line into a final geometric pattern. self.wait(2.0).
        
        # Highlight third lecture line and revert second
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), # Green
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Create a final geometric pattern (Decagon with diagonals)
        pattern = RegularPolygon(n=10, color="#00FF00").scale(1.5)
        self.place_in_area(pattern, "B2", "F6")
        
        # Adding diagonals for visual complexity
        vertices = pattern.get_vertices()
        diagonals = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(vertices)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(vertices)):
                diagonals.add(Line(vertices[i], vertices[j], stroke_width=0.5, color="#00FF00", stroke_opacity=0.4))
        
        final_visual = VGroup(pattern, diagonals)
        
        # Fade out elements and show final pattern
        self.play(
            FadeOut(points),
            FadeOut(line),
            FadeOut(imo_text),
            FadeIn(final_visual),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Final indication of the beauty
        self.play(Indicate(final_visual, color="#00FF00", scale_factor=1.1))
        
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "No three points lie on a single straight line.",
            "The line rotates until it strikes exactly one point.",
            "The pivot immediately shifts to this new point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED_COLOR)
        
        # Show 3 points in a triangle then make them collinear to show invalidity
        p1 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p2 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p3 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Start in triangle
        self.place_at_grid(p1, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(p2, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(p3, "D3")
        
        points = VGroup(p1, p2, p3)
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Move to collinear position (B3, B4, B5) to demonstrate the "invalid" condition
        self.play(
            p1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]),
            p2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            p3.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Draw invalid line and X
        invalid_line = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B6"], color=RED_COLOR)
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT + UP, RIGHT + DOWN, color=RED_COLOR),
            Line(LEFT + DOWN, RIGHT + UP, color=RED_COLOR)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(self.grid["B4"])
        
        self.play(Create(invalid_line))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(points), FadeOut(invalid_line), FadeOut(cross))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # Setup for rotation
        pivot_dot = Dot(color=GOLD_COLOR)
        target_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        other_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_dot, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(other_dot, "B5")
        
        # Rotation mechanics
        # Starting angle slightly counter-clockwise from target
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5) 
        
        # The line rotates clockwise around a single pivot point
        windmill_line = Line(LEFT * 4, RIGHT * 4, color=GOLD_COLOR)
        windmill_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_dot.get_center()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pivot_dot), FadeIn(target_dot), FadeIn(other_dot))
        self.add(windmill_line)
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Target angle calculation (D5 relative to C3)
        # C3 is (2.5, 0.2), D5 is (4.5, -0.8)
        # dx = 2.0, dy = -1.0
        target_angle = np.arctan2(-1.0, 2.0)
        
        # Rotate clockwise (decrease angle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_COLOR)
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: Pacing after significant transition
        
        # Highlight intersection
        self.play(Indicate(target_dot, color=GREEN_COLOR))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Pivot immediately shifts to this new point
        # We move the pivot dot and transition the line color
        self.play(
            pivot_dot.animate.move_to(target_dot.get_center()),
            windmill_line.animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR),
            FadeOut(target_dot, run_time=0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        )
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight each point in sequence as the line passes through it during the rotation.
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

        # Indicate points in order of being 'visited' by the line

        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p1, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p3, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Indicate(p4, color=GOLD_LINE))
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Flash all points in green (#00FF00) to signify the proof is complete.

        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN_PT)

            *[Flash(p, color=GREEN_PT) for p in points],
            *[p.animate.set_color(GREEN_PT) for p in points],

        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section data
        title_text = "Introduction: The Infinite Spinner"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine points like stars scattered across a map.",
            "We place a rotating line through one central point.",
            "As the line spins, it strikes another point.",
            "The pivot point then jumps to this new star.",
            "Can this simple dance visit every single point?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Define point positions on the grid (A2 to E6 as per Issue 21)
        # Avoid Column 1 (x=0.5) to prevent overlap with lecture
        p1_pos = self.grid['C3'] # Central point (Initial Pivot)
        p2_pos = self.grid['B2']
        p3_pos = self.grid['D5']
        p4_pos = self.grid['F4']
        p5_pos = self.grid['B6']
        
        points = VGroup(
            Dot(p1_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p2_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p3_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p4_pos, color="#FFFFFF"),
            Dot(p5_pos, color="#FFFFFF")
        )

        # Issue 22: Ensure central point is anchored properly
        self.place_at_grid(points[0], 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in 5 points at random positions (color: #FFFFFF). self.wait(1.5).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            FadeIn(points)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Create a long line through a central point (color: #FFD700). self.wait(2.0).
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        # We'll use a local copy for the pivot coordinate that we can update
        current_pivot_coord = p1_pos.copy()
        
        # Issue 20: Keep line within grid bounds (A1-F6, scale 0.9)
        # Grid width is 5. Max line half-length 2.25.
        line_half_length = 2.25
        
        windmill_line = Line(
            current_pivot_coord - np.array([1, 0, 0]) * line_half_length,
            current_pivot_coord + np.array([1, 0, 0]) * line_half_length,
            color="#FFD700"
        )
        
        def windmill_updater(mob):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            start = current_pivot_coord - direction * line_half_length
            end = current_pivot_coord + direction * line_half_length
            mob.set_points_as_corners([start, end])
            
        windmill_line.add_updater(windmill_updater)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
            Create(windmill_line)
        )
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Rotate the line clockwise; when it hits another point, flash that point (color: #00FF00). self.wait(1.5).
        # Vector P1->P3 (C3 to D5) is (2.0, -1.0). Angle is atan2(-1, 2)
        target_angle_1 = np.arctan2(-1.0, 2.0) # Clockwise from 0
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_1),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=rate_functions.linear
        )
        # Flash the hit point (P3)
        self.play(Indicate(points[2], color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Shift the line's pivot point to the hit point and continue rotation. self.wait(2.0).
        # Update current_pivot_coord in-place
        current_pivot_coord[:] = p3_pos
        
        # Next target: P4 (F4). Vector P3->P4 is (-1.0, -2.0). Angle is atan2(-2, -1)
        target_angle_2 = np.arctan2(-2.0, -1.0)
        # Ensure clockwise (decreasing)
        while target_angle_2 > target_angle_1:
            target_angle_2 -= TAU
            
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle_2),
            run_time=3.0,
            rate_func=rate_functions.linear
        )
        # Flash the new hit point (P4)
        self.play(Indicate(points[3], color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight all points with a pulsing glow to indicate potential visitation (color: #FF4500). self.wait(2.0).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            *[Indicate(p, color="#FF4500") for p in points]
        )
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Layout
        title_text = "Conclusion and Application"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Local rules create a beautiful, predictable global cycle.",
            "- This visual logic solved the hardest IMO 2011 problem.",
            "- Simple rotations reveal deep truths in geometry and combinatorics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a fast-motion animation of a 10-point windmill [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/windmill.svg]
        # completing a full cycle. self.wait(2.0).
        
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF") # Cyan
        
        # Asset: windmill.svg icon
        windmill_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/windmill.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(windmill_icon, "A1", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(windmill_icon)
        
        # Define 10 points in the visual area (B2 to F6)
        point_coords = [
            self.grid["B3"] + [0.2, 0.3, 0],
            self.grid["B5"] + [-0.1, -0.2, 0],
            self.grid["C2"] + [0.4, 0.1, 0],
            self.grid["C5"] + [-0.3, 0.5, 0],
            self.grid["D3"] + [0.5, -0.4, 0],
            self.grid["D6"] + [-0.2, 0.2, 0],
            self.grid["E2"] + [0.3, 0.6, 0],
            self.grid["E4"] + [0.1, -0.3, 0],
            self.grid["F3"] + [-0.4, 0.2, 0],
            self.grid["F5"] + [-0.1, -0.5, 0],
        ]
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(coord, color="#00FFFF", radius=0.08) for coord in point_coords])
        self.add(points)
        
        # Initial pivot point
        pivot_idx = 2 # Start at C2
        points[pivot_idx].set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta for pivot
        
        # Rotating line
        line = Line(points[pivot_idx].get_center() - 2.5*RIGHT, points[pivot_idx].get_center() + 2.5*RIGHT, color="#FFFFFF")
        line.set_stroke(width=2)
        self.add(line)
        
        # Fast-motion pivot sequence simulation
        pivots_seq = [5, 7, 1, 9, 0] # Sequence of indices for "hitting" points
        for next_p in pivots_seq:
            # Rotate around current pivot
            self.play(Rotate(line, angle=PI/2, about_point=points[pivot_idx].get_center()), run_time=0.3, rate_func=linear)
            # Switch pivot "instantly"
            self.play(
                points[pivot_idx].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
                points[next_p].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
                line.animate.move_to(points[next_p].get_center()),
                run_time=0.1
            )
            pivot_idx = next_p
            
        # Final rotation to finish the "cycle"
        self.play(Rotate(line, angle=PI, about_point=points[pivot_idx].get_center()), run_time=0.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display the text 'IMO 2011 Problem 2' in gold (#FFD700) alongside a medal icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/medal.svg].
        
        # Highlight second lecture line and revert first
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), # Gold
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Fix Issue 35: Position label in area A1-A6
        imo_text = Text("IMO 2011 Problem 2", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(imo_text, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Asset: medal.svg icon
        medal_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/medal.svg")
        medal_icon.scale(0.3)
        medal_icon.next_to(imo_text, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(imo_text),
            FadeIn(medal_icon)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out the points and line into a final geometric pattern. self.wait(2.0).
        
        # Highlight third lecture line and revert second
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), # Green
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Create a final geometric pattern (Decagon with diagonals)
        pattern_inner = RegularPolygon(n=10, color="#00FF00")
        # Fix Issue 36: Position pattern in area B1-F6
        self.place_in_area(pattern_inner, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Adding diagonals
        vertices = pattern_inner.get_vertices()
        diagonals = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(vertices)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(vertices)):
                diagonals.add(Line(vertices[i], vertices[j], stroke_width=0.5, color="#00FF00", stroke_opacity=0.4))
        
        final_visual = VGroup(pattern_inner, diagonals)
        
        # Fade out elements and show final pattern
        self.play(
            FadeOut(points),
            FadeOut(line),
            FadeOut(imo_text),
            FadeOut(medal_icon),
            FadeOut(windmill_icon),
            FadeIn(final_visual),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Final indication - [L004] use Indicate
        self.play(Indicate(final_visual, color="#00FF00", scale_factor=1.1))
        
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "Prerequisite: The Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "No three points lie on a single straight line.",
            "The line rotates until it strikes exactly one point.",
            "The pivot immediately shifts to this new point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        GOLD_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED_COLOR)
        
        # Show 3 points in a triangle - Fix per Issue 25
        p1 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p2 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        p3 = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Triangle positions from Issue 25
        self.place_at_grid(p1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(p2, "C6")
        self.place_at_grid(p3, "D4")
        
        points = VGroup(p1, p2, p3)
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Move to collinear position (B4, B5, B6) to demonstrate the "invalid" condition
        # This keeps the objects further from the lecture area per Issue 25
        self.play(
            p1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B4"]),
            p2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]),
            p3.animate.move_to(self.grid["B6"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Draw invalid line and X
        # Line from B3 to B6+ (x=2.5 to x=6.0)
        invalid_line = Line(self.grid["B3"], self.grid["B6"] + RIGHT * 0.5, color=RED_COLOR)
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT + UP, RIGHT + DOWN, color=RED_COLOR),
            Line(LEFT + DOWN, RIGHT + UP, color=RED_COLOR)
        ).scale(0.3).move_to(self.grid["B5"])
        
        self.play(Create(invalid_line))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Clean up
        self.play(FadeOut(points), FadeOut(invalid_line), FadeOut(cross))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD_COLOR)
        self.wait(1.5) 
        
        # Setup for rotation - Fix per Issue 23 and 24
        pivot_dot = Dot(color=GOLD_COLOR)
        target_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        other_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_COLOR)
        
        # Positioned far enough right to avoid overlap
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_dot, "C4")  # Issue 23 fix
        self.place_at_grid(target_dot, "D6") # Issue 24 fix
        self.place_at_grid(other_dot, "B6")  # Issue 24 fix
        
        # Rotation mechanics
        # Starting angle slightly counter-clockwise from target (approx 0.5 rad above horiz)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0.5) 
        
        # The line rotates clockwise around a single pivot point
        # Use length 6 (3 each way) so centered at C4 (x=3.5) it spans x=0.5 to x=6.5
        windmill_line = Line(LEFT * 3, RIGHT * 3, color=GOLD_COLOR)
        windmill_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_dot.get_center()))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pivot_dot), FadeIn(target_dot), FadeIn(other_dot))
        self.add(windmill_line)
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Target angle calculation (D6 relative to C4)
        # C4 is (3.5, 0.2), D6 is (5.5, -0.8)
        # dx = 2.0, dy = -1.0
        target_angle = np.arctan2(-1.0, 2.0)
        
        # Rotate clockwise (decrease angle) using rate_functions.linear per [L024]
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN_COLOR)
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Highlight intersection using Indicate per [L004]
        self.play(Indicate(target_dot, color=GREEN_COLOR))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Pivot immediately shifts to this new point
        self.play(
            pivot_dot.animate.move_to(target_dot.get_center()),
            windmill_line.animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR),
            FadeOut(target_dot, run_time=0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # New line rotation around the new pivot
        windmill_line.clear_updaters()
        windmill_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_dot.get_center()))
        
        # Continue clockwise rotation
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle - 1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Final cleanup/reset colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # === Fetching data ===
        title_text = "The Mechanism of the Pivot"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Watch the line sweep across the plane like radar.",
            "Upon impact, the center of rotation instantly changes.",
            "The clockwise motion remains constant throughout the dance."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Visual Assets ===
        # Points at grid locations requested in issues 26, 27, 28 (L002: Avoid Col 1)
        p1 = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        p2 = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        p3 = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(p1, "C3") # Issue 26: Moved from C2 to C3 to avoid lecture obstruction
        self.place_at_grid(p2, "E5") # Issue 27: Moved from D4 to E5 for better spacing
        self.place_at_grid(p3, "B6") # Issue 28: Moved from B5 to B6 for better coverage
        
        # Labels scaled and positioned (L002)
        p1_label = Text("P1", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.8).next_to(p1, UP, buff=0.1)
        p2_label = Text("P2", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.8).next_to(p2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        p3_label = Text("P3", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.8).next_to(p3, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        points_group = VGroup(p1, p2, p3, p1_label, p2_label, p3_label)
        self.add(points_group)
        
        # Animation state tracking
        state = {"pivot": p1}
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(90 * DEGREES) # Start pointing UP
        
        # Primary rotating line (L027: Persistent mobject + updater)
        line = Line(start=LEFT*5, end=RIGHT*5, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=3)

The updated Manim code for **Section 5: The 180-Degree Flip** has been implemented. 

### Key Improvements:
- **Strict Grid Alignment**: Following the VideoCritic feedback, the central pivot is now anchored at `D3`, side labels 'L' and 'R' at `D2` and `D4`, and point groups within the `B2-C2` and `E4-F4` areas.
- **Dynamic Orientation**: The 'L' and 'R' labels now move with the rotating line using updaters, clearly demonstrating the "reversal" of orientation after a 180-degree turn.
- **Visual Clarity**: Used `place_at_grid` and `place_in_area` as requested to ensure appropriate spacing and avoid overlap with lecture text.
- **Script Alignment**: Animations are synchronized with the lecture lines, specifically highlighting the "crossing" event to explain why the windmill must visit every point.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from shared state
        title = "The 180-Degree Flip"
        lecture_lines = [
            "After a half-rotation, the line returns to its angle.",
            "However, the line is now oriented in reverse.",
            "Points originally on the left are now on the right.",
            "Every point must cross the line to swap sides.",
            "This proves the windmill hits every star eventually."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors (L008)
        BLUE_PT = "#0000FF"
        RED_PT = "#FF0000"
        GOLD_LINE = "#FFD700"
        GREEN_PT = "#00FF00"
        WHITE_HEX = "#FFFFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the initial balanced line with labeled sides and colored points
        
        # Visual elements following VideoCritic suggestions (Issue 32, 33, 34)
        pivot_dot = Dot(color=WHITE_HEX, radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_dot, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        pivot_pos = pivot_dot.get_center()
        
        # Blue dots on the left (Issue 33)
        blue_dot1 = Dot(color=BLUE_PT, radius=0.08)
        blue_dot2 = Dot(color=BLUE_PT, radius=0.08)
        blue_dots = VGroup(blue_dot1, blue_dot2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(blue_dots, "B2", "C2", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Red dots on the right (Issue 33)
        red_dot1 = Dot(color=RED_PT, radius=0.08)
        red_dot2 = Dot(color=RED_PT, radius=0.08)
        red_dots = VGroup(red_dot1, red_dot2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(red_dots, "E4", "F4", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Labels (Issue 32)
        label_l = Text("L", font_size=24, color=BLUE_PT)
        label_r = Text("R", font_size=24, color=RED_PT)
        self.place_at_grid(label_l, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_r, "D4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Initial line (start vertical)
        line = Line(pivot_pos + DOWN*3, pivot_pos + UP*3, color=GOLD_LINE, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(pivot_dot), 
            FadeIn(blue_dots), 
            FadeIn(red_dots), 
            Create(line), 
            Write(label_l), 
            Write(label_r)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Rotate the line slowly 180 degrees using a 'smooth' rate function
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_HEX)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updaters for rotation (L010/L011)
        def line_updater(m):
            angle = PI/2 + angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            m.put_start_and_end_on(pivot_pos - 3.5 * direction, pivot_pos + 3.5 * direction)
            
        def labels_updater(vgroup):
            angle = PI/2 + angle_tracker.get_value()
            # Normal vector for 'Left' side relative to the line direction
            normal = np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            # Using Proximity Rule (L002) - approx 1 unit distance
            vgroup[0].move_to(pivot_pos + normal * 1.0)
            vgroup[1].move_to(pivot_pos - normal * 1.0)
            
        labels_vgroup = VGroup(label_l, label_r)
        line.add_updater(line_updater)
        labels_vgroup.add_updater(labels_updater)
        
        # Perform 180-degree rotation (PI radians)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=5, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(3.0)
        
        line.clear_updaters()
        labels_vgroup.clear_updaters()
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Morph the side labels and point colors to show the sides have completely swapped.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_HEX)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_PT)
        
        # Swap colors visually to represent the change in state relative to the line orientation
        self.play(
            blue_dots.animate.set_color(RED_PT),
            red_dots.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            label_l.animate.set_color(RED_PT),
            label_r.animate.set_color(BLUE_PT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight each point in sequence as the line passes through it.
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_HEX)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GOLD_LINE)
        
        # Indicate points to represent their crossing event
        all_stars = [blue_dot1, blue_dot2, red_dot1, red_dot2]
        for star in all_stars:
            self.play(Indicate(star, color=GOLD_LINE, scale_factor=1.5), run_time=0.8)
        
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Flash all points in green (#00FF00) to signify the proof is complete.
        
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE_HEX)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN_PT)
        
        all_points = VGroup(pivot_dot, *all_stars)
        self.play(
            *[Flash(p, color=GREEN_PT) for p in all_points],
            all_points.animate.set_color(GREEN_PT),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2.0)
```

outline.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
outline.content: Introduce the core insight needed to solve the problem: The 'Side-Count'. If we choose a line that splits the points into two equal (or near-equal) sets, what happens to that count when the line pivots?
outline.example: Visual: Color points on the 'left' side of the line Blue and points on the 'right' side Red. When the line pivots on Point P to hit Point Q, Point P moves to the other side of the line, and Point Q moves to the pivot. The total number of points on each side stays exactly the same!

storyboard.title: The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line
lecture_lines: Color points on each side of the line differently.
Pick a line splitting points into two equal sets.
As the line pivots, points swap sides across it.
The current pivot and the new pivot trade places.
The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced.
animations: Draw a balanced line through a pivot with 2 blue points (#0000FF) on the left and 2 red points (#FF0000) on the right. self.wait(2.0).
Use blue and red SurroundingRectangles to group the points on either side. self.wait(1.5).
Rotate the line; show the current pivot moving to the other side as the new point becomes the pivot. self.wait(2.0).
Use Arrows to show the points effectively exchanging places relative to the line. self.wait(1.5).
Flash the blue and red groups to show the total counts (2 on each side) remain unchanged. self.wait(2.0).

        # Points setup - avoiding collinearity for clear rotation
        pivot_p = Dot(color=WHITE_CLR)
        blue_1 = Dot(color=BLUE_CLR)
        blue_2 = Dot(color=BLUE_CLR)
        red_1 = Dot(color=RED_CLR)
        red_2 = Dot(color=RED_CLR)

        # Positioning using the 6x6 grid system (Rule L002)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_p, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_2, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(red_1, 'B4')

        windmill_line = Line(

            self.grid['F3'] + DOWN*0.5,

        )
        
        self.add(all_points)
        self.play(Create(windmill_line))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):

        # Title and lecture lines from shared state
        title_text = "The Hidden Invariant: The 'Balanced' Line"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Color points on each side of the line differently.",

            "The current pivot and the new pivot trade places.",
            "The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced."

        pivot_p = Dot(color=WHITE_CLR)
        blue_1 = Dot(color=BLUE_CLR)
        blue_2 = Dot(color=BLUE_CLR)
        red_1 = Dot(color=RED_CLR)

        # Positioning using the 6x6 grid system (Rule L002)

        self.place_at_grid(pivot_p, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_1, 'B2')

        )

        self.play(Create(windmill_line))
        self.wait(2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_CLR)

        blue_group = VGroup(blue_1, blue_2)

        rect_red = SurroundingRectangle(red_group, color=RED_CLR, buff=0.2)
        
        # Issue 31: blue_count at A2, scaled to 0.7
        blue_count = Text("2", color=BLUE_CLR, font_size=24)

        red_count = Text("2", color=RED_CLR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(red_count, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_CLR)

        def line_updater(l):

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_CLR)

        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_to_red1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Swap colors and pivot position
        # The line will automatically update its position because of the updater on pivot_pos_tracker
        self.play(
            pivot_p.animate.set_color(RED_CLR),
            red_1.animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR),
            pivot_pos_tracker.animate.move_to(red_1.get_center()),
            FadeOut(arrow_to_red1),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        
        # Continue rotation to show it's now pivoting around red_1
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(angle_tracker.get_value() - PI/6), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "The total count on each side remains perfectly balanced."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW_CLR)
        
        # New visual groups showing count preservation
        new_blue_group = VGroup(blue_1, blue_2)
        new_red_group = VGroup(pivot_p, red_2)
        
        rect_blue_f = SurroundingRectangle(new_blue_group, color=BLUE_CLR, buff=0.2)
        rect_red_f = SurroundingRectangle(new_red_group, color=RED_CLR, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_blue_f), Create(rect_red_f))
        # Use Indicate for pulsing (L004)
        self.play(Indicate(blue_count, color=YELLOW_CLR), Indicate(red_count, color=YELLOW_CLR))
        self.wait(2.0)
        
        # Clean up updater
        windmill_line.remove_updater(line_updater)
